newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dawdle over freeze, road-show.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dawdle over freeze, road-show.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds were little changed in quiet trading on Thursday as the market held its breath for Russia's Eurobond road-show and waited for the problem of frozen bonds to be solved, dealers said.

"I have not seen such a quiet day for a long time. The market has a wait-and-see attitude, waiting for them to fix the problem of frozen MinFins and for the road-show to come to London (on Friday)," a London bank dealer said.
An International Moscow Bank dealer said: "It looks like Russians are mainly selling, while the West is buying but not actively. The volume has been quite low today."
He said some selling was seen in the fourth and fifth tranches, with trading mainly conducted through brokers, to reduce the risk of obtaining paper frozen by the Russian authorities.
Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said on Thursday he was confident the problem of frozen MinFin bonds would be resolved once legal contradictions were sorted out.
"There is nothing new in what he said. The market is waiting for them to really do something," the London bank dealer said.
